subject: Physics
prompt: SI unit of stress is?
explain: Stress = Force/Area; unit is Pa (N/m²), same as pressure.

subject: Physics
prompt: Young's modulus Y is defined as?
explain: Y relates longitudinal (tensile/compressive) stress to longitudinal strain.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bulk modulus B is defined as?
explain: Bulk modulus = volumetric stress / volumetric strain; negative sign since ΔV is negative.

subject: Physics
prompt: Modulus of rigidity (shear modulus) η relates?
explain: η = shear stress / shear strain; relevant for shape changes at constant volume.

subject: Physics
prompt: Poisson's ratio σ is defined as?
explain: Poisson's ratio = lateral contraction strain / longitudinal extension strain (magnitude).

subject: Physics
prompt: Theoretical range of Poisson's ratio σ for isotropic material?
explain: Thermodynamic stability requires −1 ≤ σ ≤ 0.5; most materials have 0 < σ < 0.5.

subject: Physics
prompt: Elastic potential energy stored per unit volume?
explain: Energy density u = ½σε = stress²/(2Y) = ½Yε².

subject: Physics
prompt: Total elastic PE stored in a wire of length L, area A?
explain: U = ½ × load × extension; also equals ½ F ΔL for linear elastic deformation.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation connecting Y, B, and σ?
explain: Y = 3B(1−2σ) relates Young's modulus, bulk modulus, and Poisson's ratio.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation connecting Y, η, and σ?
explain: Y = 2η(1+σ) connects Young's modulus, shear modulus, and Poisson's ratio.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between Y, B, and η?
explain: The standard relation: 9/Y = 3/η + 1/B linking all three elastic moduli.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a perfectly rigid body, Young's modulus Y is?
explain: Rigid body has zero strain for any stress → Y = stress/strain → ∞.

subject: Physics
prompt: Hooke's law is valid up to which point on stress-strain curve?
explain: Hooke's law (stress ∝ strain) holds strictly only up to the proportionality limit.

subject: Physics
prompt: Beyond elastic limit, the material shows?
explain: Beyond elastic limit, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs; material doesn't recover fully.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which has the highest Young's modulus among common materials?
explain: Steel has Y ≈ 2×10¹¹ Pa, highest among common structural materials in JEE context.

subject: Physics
prompt: For an incompressible material, Poisson's ratio σ = ?
explain: Incompressible → ΔV = 0 → 1−2σ = 0 → σ = 0.5.

subject: Physics
prompt: Compressibility is defined as?
explain: Compressibility K = 1/B; unit is Pa⁻¹. Fluids have finite compressibility.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bulk modulus of an ideal gas at pressure P (isothermal)?
explain: Isothermal: PV = const → B = P. Adiabatic B = γP.

subject: Physics
prompt: Dimensional formula of Young's modulus?
explain: Y = stress = Force/Area → [MLT⁻²/L²] = ML⁻¹T⁻².

subject: Physics
prompt: Elongation ΔL of a wire of length L, area A, Young's modulus Y under load F?
explain: From Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) → ΔL = FL/(AY).

subject: Physics
prompt: Stress in a wire due to temperature change ΔT (ends fixed)?
explain: Thermal strain = αΔT; since ends are fixed, stress = Y × αΔT (thermal stress).

subject: Physics
prompt: Which point on stress-strain curve represents permanent set?
explain: At yield point, plastic deformation begins; permanent set (residual strain) first appears.

subject: Physics
prompt: For shear deformation, shear strain φ is defined as?
explain: Shear strain = tangential displacement x divided by perpendicular height h (= tan φ ≈ φ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Rubber has very small Young's modulus because?
explain: Rubber is highly flexible; it undergoes large deformation for small applied stress → small Y.

subject: Physics
prompt: Breaking stress depends on?
explain: Breaking stress is an intrinsic material property (stress = F/A at fracture), independent of dimensions.

subject: Physics
prompt: Proportional limit on stress-strain curve is where?
explain: Proportional limit is the point up to which stress is directly proportional to strain (Hooke's law holds).

subject: Physics
prompt: Elastic limit is the point beyond which?
options: Material doesn't return to original shape
explain: Beyond elastic limit, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs; material won't fully recover on unloading.

subject: Physics
prompt: Yield point on stress-strain curve is characterised by?
options: Large strain with little/no stress increase
explain: At yield point, material elongates considerably without significant increase in stress (plastic flow starts).

subject: Physics
prompt: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) on stress-strain curve represents?
explain: UTS is the maximum engineering stress on the stress-strain curve, after which necking begins.

subject: Physics
prompt: Lateral strain for a wire stretched along its length is?
explain: Lateral strain = –(change in diameter)/(original diameter); negative because diameter decreases on stretching.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a wire, if longitudinal strain is ε, lateral strain is –σε; volume strain is?
explain: Volume strain = longitudinal + 2×lateral = ε − 2σε = ε(1−2σ) for a stretched wire.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which material is more elastic: steel or rubber?
options: Steel (higher Y, less strain per stress)
explain: Elasticity means tendency to restore; steel has higher Y so resists deformation more — it is more elastic.

subject: Physics
prompt: Elongation of a wire under its own weight (density ρ, length L, Y)?
explain: Self-weight acts at CG; effective load = Mg/2, giving ΔL = ρgL²/(2Y) for uniform wire.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two wires series (same F): effective spring constant k_eff?
explain: Wires in series add extensions, so spring constants combine reciprocally like resistors in series.

subject: Physics
prompt: Two wires parallel (same ΔL): effective spring constant k_eff?
explain: Parallel wires share load at same extension; spring constants add directly.

subject: Physics
prompt: Spring constant of a wire (Y, A, L) is?
explain: From F = YA(ΔL)/L, comparing with F = kΔL gives k = YA/L.

subject: Physics
prompt: If wire length doubles (same material, same radius), its spring constant?
explain: k = YA/L; doubling L halves k, since Y and A are unchanged.

subject: Physics
prompt: If wire radius doubles (same L, material), spring constant changes by factor?
explain: k = YA/L ∝ r²; doubling r makes r² four times, so k becomes 4 times.

subject: Physics
prompt: Elastic potential energy per unit volume in terms of stress S and strain e?
explain: Energy density u = ½ × stress × strain = S²/(2Y) = ½Ye² — all equivalent forms.

subject: Physics
prompt: Bulk modulus of an ideal gas under adiabatic process is?
explain: Adiabatic bulk modulus = γP (ratio of specific heats × pressure); isothermal B = P.

subject: Physics
prompt: Ratio B_adiabatic / B_isothermal for an ideal gas equals?
explain: B_ad = γP and B_iso = P, so their ratio = γ. This is why speed of sound uses γP.

subject: Physics
prompt: Thermal stress in a rod of Y, α when heated by ΔT (ends fixed)?
explain: Fixed ends prevent expansion; compressive thermal stress = YαΔT develops in the rod.

subject: Physics
prompt: A ductile material compared to brittle on stress-strain graph shows?
explain: Ductile materials have a large plastic region (e.g., copper); brittle materials fracture just after elastic limit.

subject: Physics
prompt: Brittleness means a material fractures?
options: With little or no plastic deformation
explain: Brittle materials (glass, cast iron) break suddenly with negligible plastic deformation.

subject: Physics
prompt: Resilience is defined as elastic energy stored per unit volume up to?
explain: Modulus of resilience = area under stress-strain curve up to elastic limit; energy stored without permanent set.

subject: Physics
prompt: Toughness of a material is represented by area under stress-strain curve up to?
explain: Toughness = total energy absorbed per unit volume up to fracture; area under entire stress-strain curve.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a wire, work done in stretching by ΔL under force F is?
explain: Force increases linearly from 0 to F; work = area under F-ΔL graph = ½FΔL.

subject: Physics
prompt: Inter-atomic force is conservative, so elastic restoring force is?
explain: Elastic restoring forces arise from conservative interatomic potentials; energy stored is fully recoverable.

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation between Y, B, η (shear modulus) is?
explain: Standard elasticity relation: 9/Y = 3/η + 1/B, connecting all three moduli for isotropic solids.

subject: Physics
prompt: If σ = 0.5 (incompressible), what happens to volume strain ε(1−2σ)?
explain: At σ = 0.5: ΔV/V = ε(1−1) = 0; material deforms without any change in volume — incompressible.
